summary:
[  edit  ]
NOTE
Hardware:  This  TOP  uses the Nvidia Hardware Encoder to create the stream and therefore requires an Nvidia  GPU  and Windows to operate.
The Video Stream Out  TOP  acts as an  RTMP  or  SRT  sender, can create an  RTSP  server, to send compressed video and audio across the network. It uses Nvidia's hardware encoder. For RTSP, it can handle multiple clients connecting to it at the same time. Multiple Video Stream Out TOPs using the same port will be handled using the same underlying RTSP server. The Video Stream Out  TOP  can also be used to send a video stream through  WebRTC  video/audio tracks.
The video codecs that can be streamed out are H.264, H.265 (HEVC) and AV1. (AV1 is supported by recent NVIDIA GPUs only.). Not every streaming protocol and/or service supports every codec option.
The audio codecs that can be streamed out are MP3, AAC and Opus.
RTMP
Enhanced RTMP is also supported.
To obtain the RTMP URL stream to, you may need to search to find the correct URL depending on your location and the service you are using. This should be in the format:
{service url}/{stream key} .
For example for Twitch the URL would be something like
rtmp://live-yto.twitch.tv/app/live_1234567_sduhy3xJ1KJ34Eg6CjksdJLubFS7gtUY
For more information on different services see  RTMP .
SRT
SRT  can use either H.264 or H.265 video codec. It can also send per-frame metadata when a  CHOP  or  DAT  is specified in the Per-Frame Metadata parameter.
The SRT server is settings are controlled by URL options. E.g to create a Video Stream Out, in listener-mode you'd specify the URL:
srt://0.0.0.0:9494?mode=listener
To connect to listener in a Video Stream In  TOP , you'd do:
srt://127.0.0.1:9494?mode=caller
Either side of the connection can be the listener or the caller, it doesn't matter which is sending the video and which is receiving the video. The receiver would set their mode to be the opposite of whatever the sender is setting their mode to be.
All the options that are available are listed  here . Multiple options can be set using a & as separator. E.g
srt://127.0.0.1:9494?mode=caller&send_buffer_size=100000
SRT sent from the Video Stream Out  TOP  can include per-frame metadata making it easy to send and receive  CHOP / DAT  data in sync with video. It can be read with the  Video Stream In TOP .
RTSP
Obtain the URL to connect to the Video Steam Out  TOP 's RTSP server by using an Info  DAT  or by middle clicking on the node. It will be in the form:
rtsp://<ipaddress>:<port>/<streamName>
e.g.
rtsp://192.168.0.1:554/tdvidstream
Limitations
RTSP streaming does not support sending directly to another RTSP server via RTP.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Controls if the server is active or not. If this is Off then the port this server uses will not be tied up.

parameters.label: Mode
parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Selects if the mode works as an RTSP server, sends RTMP to a receiever such as a distribution service like YouTube or Twitch, or sends to an SRT destination.

parameters.label: RTSP Server
parameters.name: rtspserver
parameters.description: Use the RTSP and RTP protocol. More information  here .

parameters.label: RTMP Sender
parameters.name: rtmpsender
parameters.description: Use the RTMP protocol. More information  here .

parameters.label: SRT
parameters.name: srt
parameters.description: Use the SRT protocol. More information  here .

parameters.label: WebRTC
parameters.name: webrtc
parameters.description: Use a WebRTC peer. More info:  WebRTC ,  WebRTC DAT .

parameters.label: Network Port
parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The port the server should listen on. Multiple Video Stream Out TOPs can use the same port as long as each has a unique Stream Name.

parameters.label: Stream Name
parameters.name: streamname
parameters.description: The name of the stream for this node. This name is what comes after the / in the URL after the ipaddress:port combination.

parameters.label: Multi-Cast
parameters.name: multicast
parameters.description: Controls if RTSP server sends its video out using unicast or multicast UDP packets.

parameters.label: Destination URL
parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to send the SRT/RTMP stream to. For RTMP, this should be in the format of {service url}/{stream key}. For example for twitch the URL would be something like  rtmp://live-yto.twitch.tv/app/live_1234567_sduhy3xJ1KJ34Eg6CjksdJLubFS7gtUY . You may need to search to find the correct URL depending on your location and the service you are using. For SRT refer to the SRT documentation or the note at the start of this page.

parameters.label: Force IDR
parameters.name: forceidr
parameters.description: For debugging, this will force the server to create a new video keyframe to send to all the clients. If clients aren't getting proper image this can be used to attempt to fix it. If you need to use this parameter please report the case to support@derivative.ca.

parameters.label: FPS
parameters.name: fps
parameters.description: The  FPS  to send video at.

parameters.label: Video Codec
parameters.name: videocodec
parameters.description: ⊞  - Select which codec to use for encoding the stream, not every codec is compatible with every streaming protocol

parameters.label: H.264 (NVIDIA  GPU )
parameters.name: h264
parameters.description: Usable with RTMP and SRT.

parameters.label: H.265/HEVC (NVIDIA  GPU )
parameters.name: h265
parameters.description: Usable with RTMP via Enchanced RTMP, and SRT.

parameters.label: AV1 (NVIDIA  GPU )
parameters.name: av1
parameters.description: Usable with RTMP, via Enhanced RTMP.

parameters.label: Profile
parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: ⊞  - The H.264 profile to use to encode the frames. Some decoders can only support H.264 encoder at certain profiles.

parameters.label: Quality
parameters.name: quality
parameters.description: ⊞  - The quality level of the encoding.

parameters.label: Low
parameters.description: Latency, Low Quality   lowlatencylow  -

parameters.label: Low
parameters.description: Latency, Medium Quality   lowlatencymedium  -

parameters.label: Low
parameters.description: Latency, High Quality   lowlatencyhigh  -

parameters.label: High
parameters.description: Latency, Low Quality   highlatencylow  -

parameters.label: High
parameters.description: Latency, High Quality   highlatencyhigh  -

parameters.label: High
parameters.description: Latency, Ultra High Quality   highlatencyultrahigh  -

parameters.label: Keyframe  Interval
parameters.name: keyframeinterval
parameters.description: Set the keyframe interval for the encoder, in frames. This sets both the GOP length and the IDR interval. Both of these control how many frames are between each IDR (key) frame.

parameters.label: Max B-Frames
parameters.name: maxbframes
parameters.description: The maximum number of bi-directional frames that can occur between keyframes. More will increase latency but reduce bandwidth.

parameters.label: Intra-Refresh Period
parameters.name: intrarefreshperiod
parameters.description: Intra-refresh is a gradual keyframe that is applied across the image to clean up streaming artifacts over multiple frames, instead of one large keyframe. This controls the number of frames that elapse between each intra-refresh occuring.

parameters.label: Intra-Refresh Length
parameters.name: intrarefreshlength
parameters.description: The number of frames the intra-refresh will be spread out across.

parameters.label: Bitrate Mode
parameters.name: bitratemode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Chooses between constant (CBR) and variable (VBR) bit rate modes. Mode streaming services prefer a constant bit rate mode.

parameters.label: Average Bitrate (Mb/s)
parameters.name: avgbitrate
parameters.description: The target bitrate for the encoding. This is specified in Mb/s (megabits/second).

parameters.label: Max Bitrate (Mb/s)
parameters.name: maxbitrate
parameters.description: The maximum bitrate for the encoding. This is specified in Mb/s (megabits/second).

parameters.label: Num H264 Slices per  Frame
parameters.name: numslices
parameters.description: This controls how many pieces (slices) each H.264 frame is separated into. Some decoders are able to decode multiple slices simultaneously so setting this to a value above 1 allows those decoders to run more efficiently.

parameters.label: Audio  CHOP
parameters.name: audiochop
parameters.description: A timesliced audio source to send along with the video. Depending on the protocol and audio codec, you same need to resample the audio using a  Resample CHOP  to either 44100 or 48000Hz.

parameters.label: Audio Codec
parameters.name: audiocodec
parameters.description: ⊞  - The audio codec to compress the audio to.

parameters.label: MP3
parameters.name: mp3
parameters.description: Compressed lossy codec. Can only do 2 channels of audio.

parameters.label: AAC
parameters.name: aac
parameters.description: AAC  is a lossy audio compression codec. Can only do 2 channels of audio. MP3 compression will not have gapless playback. Note: A particlular behavior on Windows OS AAC encoder; for 1 and 2 channels the selection of bit rate is for both channels combined. i.e. it’s 192kb/s for one channel, or 2x96kb/s for two. However, when using more than 2 channels the bitrate is per channel ie. for 6 channel then it’s 6x192kb/s.

parameters.label: Opus
parameters.name: opus
parameters.description: Opus  is a lossy audio compression codec.

parameters.label: Audio Bit Rate
parameters.name: audiobitrate
parameters.description: ⊞  - Set the bit rate used for encoding audio.

parameters.label: Include Silent Audio Stream
parameters.name: includesilentaudio
parameters.description: ⊞  - Some broadcasting services require an audio stream to be included. This will include a silent audio stream along with the video in the event there isn't actual audio being streamed video the  CHOP  parameter.

parameters.label: Per-Frame Metadata  CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: perframemetadata
parameters.description: Send metadata from this OP with each frame of the video stream. This data can be recevied from the  Video Stream In TOP  using an  Info CHOP  and  Info DAT .

parameters.label: Per-Frame Metadata
parameters.name: perframemetadata
parameters.description: Send metadata from this OP with each frame of the video stream. This data can be received from the  Video Stream In TOP  using an  Info CHOP  and  Info DAT .

parameters.label: WebRTC
parameters.name: webrtc
parameters.description: Set the  WebRTC DAT  (ie. peer) to send the video stream over. Setting this will automatically populate the WebRTC Connection parameter menu with available connections.

parameters.label: WebRTC Connection
parameters.name: webrtcconnection
parameters.description: Select the  WebRTC  peer-to-peer connection. Selecting this will automatically population the WebRTC Track parameter menu with available video output tracks.

parameters.label: WebRTC Video Track
parameters.name: webrtcvideotrack
parameters.description: Select the video output track that's a part of the WebRTC peer-to-peer connection.

parameters.label: WebRTC Audio Track
parameters.name: webrtcaudiotrack
parameters.description: Optionally select the audio output track that's a part of the WebRTC peer-to-peer connection, to be sent along with the video.

parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - quickly change the resolution of the  TOP 's data.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution.

parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.name: eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.name: quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Half
parameters.name: half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 2X
parameters.name: 2x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 4X
parameters.name: 4x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: 8X
parameters.name: 8x
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.name: fit
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Enables the  Resolution  parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: ⊞  - Enabled only when the  Resolution  parameter is set to Custom  Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.name: resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.name: custom
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.name: armenu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the  TOP .

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determine how the  TOP  image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.name: fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.name: best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.name: outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.name: nearest
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.name: linear
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get  TOP  images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native  Resolution .

parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.description: Uses   mipmap  filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.label: Passes
parameters.name: npasses
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the  TOP  the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the  TOP  will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.name: format
parameters.description: ⊞  - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to  Pixel Formats  for more information.

parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.name: useinput
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace.

parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue  Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)

parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.name: rg8fixed

parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
